_comment: Turkish terms chosen for the what-is-theory lesson. status: ok = attested in a Turkish source I opened; chosen = my own rendering of an English term (no Turkish source checked); check = only weakly attested, needs a Turkish-language reviewer. See content/research-notes/what-is-theory.md.

theory.note: Project term. ‘Teori’ also common in Turkish; the course uses ‘kuram’.

paradigm.note: Kuhn’s Turkish translation title uses ‘Bilimsel Devrimlerin Yapısı’ (publisher page: Kırmızı Yayınları, tr. Nilüfer Kuyaş).

middle-range-theory.note: ‘Orta düzey’ chosen to match the course unit title ‘Orta Düzey Etkiler’. ‘Orta boy kuramlar’ seen on a Turkish philosophy/sociology page (author Ömer Yıldırım, citing a Turkish open-education textbook, with the grand/middle/small sizes ‘büyük boy, orta boy, küçük boy’). ‘Orta erimli’ and ‘orta menzilli’ appeared only in search-engine summaries and are NOT used.

grand-theory.note: Seen in the same Turkish page title (‘Büyük Boy, Orta Boy ve Küçük Boy Kuramlar’); not opened in full.

falsifiability.note: ‘Çürütülebilirlik’ also plausible; not verified, not listed as an alternative.

media-centric.note: No Turkish source checked; ‘medya merkezli / toplum merkezli’ are the natural renderings.

administrative-research.note: ‘Yönetimsel araştırmalar’ is in the title of Erdoğan, Keloğlu-İşler and Durmuş (2005), İletişim Kuram ve Araştırma Dergisi 21. ‘İdari’ is the direct rendering used in some books but was not verified in a source I opened.

dominant-paradigm.note: ‘Egemen ve eleştirel yaklaşımlar’ is Yaylagül’s (2006) subtitle; ‘anadamar/çoğulcu’ vs ‘eleştirel/radikal’ is Yavuz (2015).

semiotic-tradition.note: Uses the core glossary’s ‘göstergebilim’ for semiotics.
